## 1. Choose a condition

Run this check first. Then change `followup` to `c(138, 132, 150, 155)`
and rerun the chunk. These observations are already matched by participant.

```{r}
baseline <- c(150, 140, 160, 155)
followup <- c(138, 132)
if (length(followup) != length(baseline)) {
  "Check the input: baseline and follow-up counts differ"
} else {
  followup - baseline
}
```

ANSWER: Why should we check the lengths before subtracting?

## 3. Read a function with checks

This helper is complete. Run it and explain the four example results.

```{r}
safe_mean <- function(x) {
  if (!is.numeric(x) || !is.null(dim(x))) {
    stop("x must be a numeric vector", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (any(is.infinite(x))) {
    stop("x must not contain infinite values", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (all(is.na(x))) return(NA_real_)
  return(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))
}

safe_mean(c(2, NA, 4))
safe_mean(numeric(0))
safe_mean(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
try(safe_mean("4"), silent = TRUE)
```

ANSWER: Which check or return handles each of these four inputs?

## 4. Reuse the function and check the result

These two calculations establish the results before refactoring.

```{r}
markers <- data.frame(
  marker_a = c(4.1, 5.2, NA, 6.0),
  marker_b = c(12, 10, 9, 11)
)
original_a <- mean(markers[["marker_a"]], na.rm = TRUE)
original_b <- mean(markers[["marker_b"]], na.rm = TRUE)
c(marker_a = original_a, marker_b = original_b)

# TODO: replace each NA_real_ with safe_mean(markers[["column_name"]]).
refactored_a <- NA_real_
refactored_b <- NA_real_
isTRUE(all.equal(refactored_a, original_a))
isTRUE(all.equal(refactored_b, original_b))
```

Both comparisons are FALSE for the placeholders. They should be TRUE after
you complete the two calls.

ANSWER: What do the comparisons tell you about the refactor?
